The proposal only takes a slightly lower rate.

It is clear ZCG/ZCAP has not understood the issue. 90%+ of coinholders dislike how money is being spent (for instance, at sex conferences with sex workers representing Zcash). This bled over into holders realizing ZCG/ZCAP don't care what coinholders think.

The issue: ***there can be no taxation without representation***. ZCAP is an insular group. ZCG spent 100s of millions in todays dollars on ZSAs which the community voted down by 90% and then kept spending money on it. ZCAP elects ZCG, and ZCG spends block rewards with no coinholder representation. It's a parasitical system and this flaw is deeply immoral when trying to sell Zcash as money.

Maxime has done an outstanding job at documenting ZCAP's spending.

We don't want the coffers drawn down less, we want to end the block subsidy going to ZCAP/ZCG so that Zcash can be sold as fair money.

The original post does nothing to alleviate our concerns - there can be no taxation without representation in a fair money system.

I strongly object to this proposal.

Not only does it ***extend*** ZCG's mandate until 2032, it also does not solve the actual issues at hand.

ZCG allocated a $455K grant to ZSAs using coinholder money, ***after*** coinholders voted at 98.6% against ZSAs. This is unacceptable.

**Our money is, as we speak, actively being deployed against our own interests.** Coinholders are paying for these grants, are paying for the salaries of ZCG committee members, and are the end users. They should be in control.

> "It is hard to imagine a more stupid or more dangerous way of making decisions than by putting those decisions in the hands of people who pay no price for being wrong." — Thomas Sowell

The reality is that no committee, whether elected by ZCAP or coinholders, can prosper. Committees never work. ZCG is akin to central planning in communist regimes, it cannot work.

The only acceptable solution is to **completely abolish ZCG**. Let the free market handle it.
